entities.summary:
The Wikimedia Foundation is a prominent American charitable organization headquartered in San Francisco, California. Founded in 2003 by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger, it has revolutionized the way people access and contribute to knowledge. The foundation's mission to make knowledge freely available to everyone has had far-reaching consequences, particularly in the digital age.

The Wikimedia Foundation's significance lies in its role as a catalyst for collaborative knowledge-sharing. It has enabled millions of users worldwide to create, edit, and share content on Wikipedia, thereby democratizing access to information. This has not only transformed the way we consume knowledge but also had a profound impact on education, research, and cultural preservation.

The foundation's legacy is evident in its success in creating a global network of contributors and users. Its efforts have also inspired new models for collaborative content creation and open-source innovation. Furthermore, the Wikimedia Foundation has played a crucial role in promoting digital literacy and critical thinking skills, particularly among underrepresented communities.

The Wikimedia Foundation's impact can be seen in various statistics: over 50 million registered users contribute to Wikipedia every month, with millions more accessing the platform daily. The foundation's efforts have also led to significant improvements in content quality, accuracy, and diversity.

In conclusion, the Wikimedia Foundation's influence extends beyond its own boundaries, shaping the way we interact with knowledge and each other. Its legacy will continue to be felt for generations to come.

Their legacy is studied through the lens of historical causation.", "summary": "The Wikimedia Foundation is an American non-profit organisation founded on 20 June 2003 by Wikipedia co-founder Jimmy Wales — established to host and support the free knowledge projects including Wikipedia (launched 2001), Wikimedia Commons, Wikidata, Wikisource, Wiktionary, and related sister projects. Headquartered in San Francisco, California, the Wikimedia Foundation is one of the most significant organisations in the history of the internet and of human knowledge production: Wikipedia, its primary project, has become the world's largest and most widely consulted encyclopaedia — with over 60 million articles in approximately 330 languages as of 2024, serving approximately 1.5 billion unique devices per month.

The foundation's mission is to make the sum of all human knowledge freely available to every person on the planet — a goal stated in explicitly universalist terms that has positioned the Wikimedia projects as a global public infrastructure for knowledge access. Unlike the major internet platforms (Google, Facebook, Amazon), the Wikimedia Foundation is a non-profit that operates without advertising revenue, depending entirely on donations from millions of individuals and institutional grants. This financial model — which has been periodically controversial as Wikipedia's servers and staff costs have grown — has preserved the encyclopaedia's independence from commercial pressures and advertising influence.

Wikipedia's epistemological impact on human knowledge access has been transformative: it is the first reference source consulted by hundreds of millions of people globally, it has displaced commercial encyclopaedias (Encyclopædia Britannica ceased print publication in 2012), and its collaborative authoring model — in which millions of volunteer editors create, verify, and maintain content under transparent policies — represents an entirely new model of knowledge production.
